items.title: Islamabad High Court bars FIR mention in character certificates after acquittal
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that police cannot mention an FIR in the character certificate of a citizen who has been acquitted in the case, declaring any such certificate unlawful and invalid. Justice Ayyaz Shaukat, while deciding a public interest petition, directed the Inspector General of Police, Islamabad, to establish a formal mechanism to ensure that references to criminal cases ending in acquittal are not included in character certificates issued to citizens. The court observed that citizens should not be compelled to approach courts to exercise rights already guaranteed under the law. It held that following an acquittal, there was no legal justification for portraying an individual as an accused or criminal through a police-issued character certificate. Rules such mention violates constitutional rights, including dignity and freedom of movement Allowing the petition, the court ordered the removal of a reference to an FIR registered at Shalimar Police Station from the petitioner’s character certificate. The judgement clarified that although police could maintain internal records of criminal cases for official purposes, such information could not be disclosed in character certificates issued to citizens, particularly when these were required for travelling abroad. It further observed that there was no legal basis for mentioning an FIR in a character certificate after the proceedings had culminated in a final acquittal. Any certificate containing such a reference would be legally invalid. Justice Ayyaz Shaukat also rejected the police’s description of the petitioner as having been “discharged” during the investigation, observing that such a characterisation undermined the legal effect and status of the acquittal. The court held that including an FIR in a character certificate despite an individual’s acquittal violated Articles 4, 9, 14 and 15 of the Constitution, which protect citizens’ rights, liberty, dignity and freedom of movement. It emphasised that a person acquitted through due process of law could not continue to face adverse consequences through a character certificate suggesting involvement in criminal proceedings. The court directed the Islamabad police chief to introduce a proper procedure to ensure that acquitted citizens did not have to initiate fresh litigation merely to obtain character certificates reflecting their actual legal status. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Immigration requirements hit African travellers hardest — IATA
items.description: By Dickson Omobola International Air Transport Association, IATA, has released the results of its 2026 Global Passenger Survey, GPS, revealing, among other findings, that immigration requirements have discouraged passengers from visiting certain destinations. IATA, which highlighted two other major trends in passenger behaviour and expectations, said travellers were embracing biometric identification to reduce repeated document checks and expressing strong interest in using digital passports for check-in and more personalised services during booking. The survey also found that artificial intelligence, AI, was changing how passengers planned their trips. From finding flights and comparing fares to discovering new destinations, passengers are increasingly incorporating AI into their travel planning. Speaking on the survey, IATA’s Senior Vice President, Operations, Safety and Security, Nick Careen, said: “Passengers are embracing technology to make travel easier. AI is becoming a mainstream travel planning tool, while biometrics and digital identity are creating a faster and more seamless airport experience. Yet many travellers continue to face barriers from complex immigration and visa processes. Governments can help by simplifying entry requirements, eliminating duplicate checks, and accelerating the issuance and acceptance of secure digital travel credentials.” According to the survey, nearly six in 10 passengers reported experiencing biometric identification at least once in the past 12 months, while satisfaction with the technology reached its highest level yet. Meanwhile, the survey showed that entry requirements were becoming a growing barrier to travel, even as passengers embraced technology. Immigration requirements had discouraged 43 per cent of passengers from visiting a destination, up from 33 per cent in 2025. Among passengers discouraged from travelling to a particular destination by geopolitical conflict, 72 per cent said safety was the main reason, while 13 per cent cited uncertainty over whether travel was possible. Of those deterred by immigration requirements, 53 per cent said the process was too complex. Privacy concerns and cost were less common reasons, accounting for 17 per cent each. IATA said African travellers were among the most satisfied with their travel experiences but were also the most likely to have been discouraged from visiting a destination by immigration requirements. items.title: From engineering to the pulpit: Prophet Jimmy marks 20 years in prophetic ministry
items.description: Before becoming known as Prophet Jimmy, Jimmy Alla-Mensah had built a professional career in network and security engineering, working with major organisations including Verizon and Lockheed Martin. He had invested years in education, professional development and technical certifications, particularly in Cisco networking and security. It was a career path that offered professional fulfilment and a future he believed he could predict. But in November 2006, he made a decision that would take his life in a direction he had not originally planned: entering prophetic ministry. For the US-based Ghanaian prophet, the transition was not the result of a failed career or a lack of professional opportunities. Rather, he says, it followed a growing conviction that God had a different assignment for his life. His spiritual journey had taken a significant turn on April 14, 2004, when he became born again. As his relationship with God developed, he says, so did his understanding of purpose. By November 2006, he had stepped into prophetic ministry, leaving behind the relative familiarity of the engineering profession for a calling that presented an entirely different set of demands. A different kind of preparation The transition was particularly significant because, unlike his engineering career, prophetic ministry was not something he had spent years studying or preparing for professionally. Prophet Jimmy says he entered ministry without formal prophetic training, prior ministry experience or the opportunity to understudy an experienced minister. He therefore had to learn while carrying the responsibilities of ministry, depending on prayer, Scripture study, personal discipline and experience. The experience, he says, taught him that having a calling does not automatically mean one has developed the maturity required to fulfil it. “Anointing does not eliminate the need for wisdom. A calling does not remove the need for character. And spiritual gifts do not exempt anyone from learning,” he reflects. His experience has also strengthened his appreciation for mentorship, accountability and sound biblical foundations. Beyond professional fulfilment The demands of ministry have also introduced him to challenges quite different from those he encountered in engineering. Where his previous profession involved network infrastructure, security systems and technical solutions, ministry has brought him into direct contact with people dealing with sickness, broken relationships, financial difficulties, hopelessness and spiritual struggles. He speaks of nights spent in prayer, long counselling hours, emotional exhaustion, disappointments and the responsibility of standing with people through difficult moments. Yet, he says, the opportunity to see people regain hope and find strength has given the work a different kind of meaning. “My engineering career gave me professional fulfillment. Ministry has given me the opportunity to participate in something that reaches deeply into the lives of people,” he says. He acknowledges that the joy of serving comes with sacrifices, but says he remains grateful for the privilege of serving God and people. Twenty years of a different journey The journey has not been without difficult seasons. One particularly painful experience was watching a church he had worked hard to build decline from approximately 300 congregants to about 10. The experience brought questions about failure, purpose and whether he had the strength to continue. It also taught him not to measure the success of a calling solely by attendance, popularity or public recognition. Looking back, he says he would tell his younger self to remain humble, learn from mistakes, care for his health and protect his family. He would also remind himself that ministers are human beings who sometimes need encouragement and rest. “Above all, remember that you are a human being before you are a minister,” he says. As he prepares to mark 20 years in prophetic ministry, Prophet Jimmy describes the journey as one that has tested his faith, challenged his assumptions and reshaped his understanding of leadership and service. The anniversary celebration is scheduled for Sunday, November 8, 2026, at House of Divine Glory Ministry International, 7895 Cessna Avenue, Suite B, Gaithersburg, Maryland 20879. The celebration will reflect the themes of “20 Years of Grace,” “20 Years of Ministry” and “20 Years of God’s Faithfulness.” For Prophet Jimmy, the words of 1 Samuel 7:12 capture the significance of the milestone: “HITHERTO HATH THE LORD HELPED US.”

items.title: Cost of provinces
items.description: THE cost would be steep. We all knew that. An Islamabad-based think tank has now put figures to those costs. That gives a fiscal dimension to a debate that has largely been driven by political demands and promises of better administration. The Policy Research Institute of Market Economy estimates that creating two more provinces in Punjab could add Rs47bn to Rs57bn to annual recurring expenditure. The bill could rise to Rs610bn-Rs730bn if all the country’s 30 divisional units were turned into provinces. Every new province would require a permanent administrative and political structure, including a governor, chief minister, assembly, secretariat and high court. Their salaries, operating expenses and overheads would have to be met year after year, leaving less money for development. The figures expose a major weakness in the argument for creating more provinces: political and administrative restructuring is often presented as an inexpensive way to make government more responsive. It is not. Smaller administrative units create another layer of government whose costs would be hard to justify. If a substantial portion of their allocations goes towards maintaining political and administrative establishments, little would remain for schools, hospitals and other essential services. Citizens promised better governance could end up paying for an expensive new tier without seeing much improvement. There is, of course, a real case for reorganising provincial boundaries. Punjab’s size and population, regional disparities and the sense of political and economic neglect in its southern districts cannot be dismissed. The demand for a separate South Punjab province reflects genuine grievances over unequal development. But these grievances cannot be resolved simply by creating new capitals, assemblies and secretariats. Nor should the fiscal argument be used to brush aside legitimate demands for political representation and administrative autonomy. Can the same objectives be achieved through empowered local governments? Political parties’ record of repeatedly suspending, delaying or weakening elected LGs suggests that the problem is less the size of provinces than the reluctance of political leadership to devolve power and resources. Functional LGs, with predictable funding, elected representatives and clearly defined responsibilities, could take decision-making nearer to citizens without multiplying provincial overheads. Any proposal for provincial restructuring must show how it would improve public services. It must also establish how new units would finance recurring expenditure. The creation of provinces is a long-term fiscal and constitutional commitment. Political parties demanding new provinces must explain how they intend to pay for them and what improvements citizens can expect. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: US to deport 150 Afghan immigrants back to Kabul
items.description: WASHINGTON: President Don­­ald Trump’s administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan, US media reported, a move advocacy groups say could endanger their lives. Trump last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown, and sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the August 2021 takeover by the Taliban. More than 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported in the latest push, The New York Times reported on Friday, citing three unnamed US officials, and the first flight could leave as soon as Monday. Among those expected to be deported are relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies. While the US cannot arrange deportations directly to Afgha­n­istan, the officials told the Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Kidnapping horror in Edo:Woman, fellow kidnappers caught by CCTV to die
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu WHEN Governor Monday Okpebholo was sworn-in on November 12, 2024, he was said to have confided in a close aide that there were two things he detested and would not allow them fester in Edo State: Thugerry and cultism. Closely related to this was kidnapping and other violent crimes. To show that he was prepared to check these challenges, Okpebholo approached the state House of Assembly to strengthen the anti-cultism and anti-kidnapping laws which now provide that any building linked to kidnapping and cultism would be demolished while convicted kidnappers would face the death penalty. To make justice seamless and devoid of bureaucratic encumbrances, the governor approached the Chief Judge of the state to dedicate a court to the two issues of kidnapping and cultism. The test of the resolve of the governor against kidnappers and cultism happened on the morning of Sunday, June 14, 2026 when, in broad daylight at the popular Vegetable Market off Airport Road, dare-devil kidnappers, operating in a pepper red Lexus Jeep, alighted from their vehicle, shot the tyres of a parked Toyota Highlander to kidnap the occupant. The owner of the vehicle escaped but his wife was not lucky as the kidnappers went away with her. The video of the incident went viral on social media courtesy of a CCTV in a building opposite the area where the incident happened. With marching orders from Okpebholo and the Inspector General of Police, four suspects, including a female, were arrested a few days after in connection with the incident and they became the first test of the courts dedicated to kidnapping and cultism. Barely four months after the investigation and prosecution started, the four suspects, namely, Marvelous Isaac, Wisdom Michael, Rufus Emete Michael and Gift Rachael, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Defendants, were found guilty of the Vegetable Market kidnap and three others in different parts of the state and capital and also being members of a secret cult, and sentenced to death by hanging or by lethal injection. The charge sheet was marked CD/S/06C/2026 between the state and four Defendants. The judgment was delivered on September 29, 2026 by Justice A. T. Momodu. It took Momodu over three hours, 30 minutes to deliver his judgment during which he attributed the success recorded by the prosecution to the CCTV in the opposite building and advised that there should be a deliberate effort to install them in business areas, public and even homes. He said the prosecution called seven witnesses while seven exhibits tendered in the trial of kidnapping, armed robbery, illegal possession of firearms, conspiracy, and membership of a secret cult among others. “I wish to place on record my profound appreciation to the private citizen whose CCTV captured the scene of the Vegetable Market kidnapping incident”, the trial judge said. “That singular act of installing CCTV in his premises provided evidence which assisted the police in the detection and proof of the crime that took place at the Vegetable Market, I commend him. “In this age where crime has become sophisticated, I encourage all residents of Edo State to endeavour to acquire and install CCTV cameras in their homes, shops, vehicles and business premises”. One of the highlights of the case was that the kidnappers demanded N130 million ransom from their victims’ families but got about N60 million before they met their waterloo. Evidence The prosecution said it was the June 14 footage of a video captured by a close circuit camera that went viral on the social media that captured the precise moment of the abduction at the Vegetable Market. It said the police deployed their tactical intelligence and arrested the 1st defendant on June 17 and he led detectives to their criminal hideout beside Awuze Hotel and Bar off Ekehuan Road, Benin City, where one Precious exchanged gunfire with the police. Precious was reportedly arrested with gunshot injuries and later died at the Police Hospital Benin-City. He was said to be the Chief Security Officer of his community. The 2nd Defendant, 3rd Defendant and 4th Defendant were arrested on June 20 at different locations in Edo and Delta states. Justice Momodu said when information got to the members of the public that the suspected persons who carried out the kidnap at the Vegetable Market had been arrested, persons who claimed to have fallen victim surfaced at the police station. According to him, the 1st Prosecution Witness, who was the female victim kidnapped at the Vegetable Market, testified that she knew all the offenders. She said that on their way to the forest, they picked up a lady who joined them in the vehicle whom she positively identified as the 4th Defendant. The victim said her eyes were blindfolded and was later released on Wednesday morning. “The kidnappers, whilst armed with guns, took her watch, earrings and hand chain worth over N15 million”, the judge said. “Under cross examination, the PW1 testified amongst others that, in her statement to the police, she stated that she knew the four Defendants and the various roles they played. “She recognised them as they were not masked when they kidnapped her. She also stated, in her statement to the police, the items that were taken from her and that they are worth over N15 million. The 2nd Prosecution Witness, who was the victim whose jeep they used in the Vegetable Market kidnap, testified that he knew the 1st- 4th Defendants. “On April 23, he was kidnapped from his wife’s shop and taken to the bush with his car by some gunmen and held captive for five days”, Momodu said. “The kidnappers initially asked for N30 million as ransom, but was negotiated to N5.5 million which was paid by his family before he was released on April 28 but his Lexus 350 jeep was not given to him as the kidnappers retained it in their possession before they were eventually caught by the police.” The witness stated that three boys and a lady kidnapped him and took him to the bush. He further testified that after they released him, his car remained in their possession for about a month and two weeks. According to him, he was called by a friend that the police arrested some people with a red Lexus jeep and that he should go and verify if it was his car. “At the police station, after checking the chassis number on the vehicle with his car documents, he discovered that it was his car”, the judge said. The 3rd Prosecution Witness testified that he knew the 1st – 4th Defendants. On May 26 at about 8.30pm, he was kidnapped at Ekehuan Road, by GT Bank Benin City. According to him, he stopped to say hello to his friend and barely five minutes after they exchanged pleasantries, a red Lexus 350 Jeep parked beside where his friends parked their cars. He was sitting beside the road but his friends saw two boys came down from the jeep armed with a gun and shot in his direction and they all ran. “He was shot at the second time; they caught him and blindfolded him. They laid him down at the back of the jeep with a gun pointed at his head as he was begging for his life. “They drove for hours till they got to a thick forest and demanded N100 million ransom”. He said the kidnappers called his office, family and friends and that, after negotiation, his family and friends paid N12.47 million ransom including the N35,000 cash which they removed from his pocket to the kidnappers, adding that “on May 30, in the early hours of the morning, still blindfolded, the kidnappers dropped him off with the same Lexus 350 jeep and found his way home”. According to him, after he was kidnapped, on their way, the kidnappers made a call to a certain girl who they instructed to wait for them at the junction, that they would pick her up from there, which they eventually did. “The girl is the 4th Defendant who was equally with the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Defendants in the bush”. The ransom was delivered to the kidnappers by his wife at Utagbon area, off Ekehuan road and they even used the same Lexus 350 jeep to collect the ransom.” The 4th Prosecution Witness said the 1st Prosecution Witness is his wife and he knew all the defendants and that he witnessed the incident that happened at the Vegetable Market. According to him, he had just closed from church, alongside his wife and their children waiting for a trader to bring what they ordered for when kidnappers came out from the Lexus jeep and shot at the tyre of his car. He was able to escape and ran to nearby Aideyan Police Station. The witness said that his wife ran too but they ran after her and took her away. He positively identified the four kidnappers who, according to him, were armed with pump action guns and dressed in black. He said the lady (4th Defendant) was the one who came to collect N12 million ransom at off Akenzua Close and that the 4th Defendant came with the 1st Defendant at the occasion. The 5th Prosecution Witness testified that she knew the 1st-4th Defendants, saying that on March 8 whilst at a junction around No 12, Oreoghene, Off Siluko, Benin-City, “suddenly one white vehicle blocked my vehicle, one of the kidnappers shot at my vehicle tyre while others dragged me out of my vehicle and pushed me inside the vehicle they came in and zoomed off.” The kidnappers blindfolded her and drove her to an unknown destination. On getting to the destination, she saw the other gang members whom she could identify. While in their captivity, she said they beat her up mercilessly. She stated that she was with them for five days before her family raised N25 million ransom and, after collecting the money, the gang leader handed her over to another set of kidnappers, who also relocated and held her for another six days. According to her, she was with them in the creek before they released her after collecting another ransom of N5 million from her family members. She said that the total money her family members paid the kidnappers was N30 million. The 6th Prosecution Witness, a police officer attached to Aideyan Police Station, Benin-City, gave evidence to the effect that on June 14, the husband of the woman kidnapped at the Vegetable Market reported the case at the police station after he narrowly escaped. She said that she recorded a statement from him and a team of detectives with Patrol 05 was dispatched to the scene, where two empty shells of expended cartridges were recovered. She said the victim’s car was recovered at the station for safe keeping. The 7th Prosecution Witness was the Investigating Police Officer (I.P.O) who said he had investigated several cases of kidnapping and cultism before. According to him, sequel to the viral video regarding the kidnapping incident that took place on June 14 at the Vegetable Market, Benin-City, which surfaced on social media, detectives from Force Headquarters, led by CSP Idaba Peters, arrested the 1st Defendant on the June 17, saying he led the police to their hideout beside Awuze Hotel and Bar, off Ekehuan Road, Benin-City. He said the 1st Defendant confessed that he was the gang leader of the four armed men that kidnapped at the Vegetable Market and that he had been into kidnapping for ransom for more than three years and he usually borrowed guns from the CSO of the Ureghin Community known as Liberty (Precious). The 1st Defendant, according to him, further confessed that he led the late Precious and the second defendant to the kidnap of one of the victims and collected a ransom of N12.5 million from his family members. The IPO said the 1st Defendant also confessed being a member of a secret cult, known as Eiye Confraternity. He narrated: “The 1st Defendant did confess that he escaped from the Correctional Centre, Benin-City during the EndSARS protest in 2020. “That his first kidnapping with the syndicate was the kidnap of the owner of one Lexus 350 SUV and his share of the ransom collected was N450, 000. “The 1st Defendant further confessed that his second kidnapping with the syndicate was when they kidnapped one man along Ekehuan Road, and his share from the ransom was N1 million. “He also admitted that his third kidnapping with the syndicate was when they kidnapped a woman at Vegetable Market in Benin-City and his share of the ransom of N12 million collected was N1.5 million.” Justice Momodu, in his judgment, said except the 4th Defendant, the case of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Defendants was a total denial of the charge against them. He said: “In count I, you, Marvelous Isaac, is hereby sentenced to seven years imprisonment. “In counts II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, and IX, you, Marvelous Isaac, is hereby sentenced to death by hanging or through the administration of lethal injection. “You shall be hanged by the neck till you are dead. May the Lord have mercy on your soul. “In count X, you, Marvelous Isaac, is hereby sentenced to 10 years imprisonment. “In count XI, you, Marvelous Isaac, is hereby sentenced to life imprisonment.” For the 2nd Defendant, he said: “In count I, you Wisdom Michael, is hereby sentenced to seven years imprisonment. “In counts II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII and IX, you, Wisdom Michael, is hereby sentenced to death by hanging or through the administration of lethal injection. “You shall be hanged by the neck till you are dead. May the Lord have mercy on your soul.” For the 3rd Defendant, he said, “In count I, you, Rufus Emete Michael, is hereby sentenced to seven years imprisonment. “In counts II, III, VI and VII, you, Rufus Emete Michael, is hereby sentenced to death by hanging or through the administration of lethal injection. “You shall be hanged by the neck till you are dead. May the Lord have mercy on your soul.” For the 4th Defendant, Justice Momodu said, “In count I, you, Gift Raphael, is hereby sentenced to seven years imprisonment. “In counts II, IV, VI, VII and VIII, you, Gift Raphael, is hereby sentenced to death by hanging or through the administration of lethal injection. “You shall be hanged by the neck till you are dead. May the Lord have mercy on your soul.” He ordered that all the exhibits made up of a Jojef pump action gun and two unexpended cartridges and two expended cartridges be confiscated to the Federal Government of Nigeria and are to be handed over to the Edo State Armourer of the Nigeria Police, State C.I.D. Edo State headquarters by the Deputy Director of the Criminal Division of the High Court for destruction within days. The post Kidnapping horror in Edo:Woman, fellow kidnappers caught by CCTV to die appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LPG price twice the official rate in open market
items.description: • Ogra notifies about Rs15 per kg increase in gas price • Association warns of strike from Nov 16 over new LPG policy ISLAMABAD: As the government again notified an increase in the price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for November, its price in the open market is twice as high as the official rate amid a shortage of LPG due to the US-Iran war. In a notification on Saturday, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified Rs294,075 per tonne for November compared to Rs279,341 in the previous month. Following the increase, the official retail rate of an 11.8 kg domestic cylinder of LPG is Rs3,470, up by Rs173. The official LPG rate is Rs294 per kilogramme. The oil and gas regulator said that the LPG producer price was linked with Saudi Aramco-CP and the US dollar exchange rate. It added that compared to the previous month, Saudi Aramco-CP had increased by 6.47 per cent, while the average dollar exchange rate had slightly decreased by 0.12pc, resulting in an increase in the LPG consumer price by Rs14.73 per kg. In the open market, LPG is selling for up to Rs630 per kg, while the company-operated franchises are charging up to Rs400 per kg, with many warning that the crisis would compound due to the gas shortage. LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan Chairman Irfan Khokhar said that the situation was serious because of the Iran border closure . He said at least 70 per cent of LPG was imported from Iran, while only 30pc was locally produced. “The government has to make serious efforts to control market manipulations,” Mr Khokhar added. On the other hand, LPG marketing companies thre­atened to shut down their businesses from Nov 16 if the private sector was sidelined in the upcoming LPG policy. Pakistan LPG Marketers Association Cha­irman Ali Haider warned that they will observe a strike from Nov 16 if the government implemented the policy. He said the government should not reverse the deregulation of LPG, adding that the gas was in short supply due to the Iran border closure. “Out of around 1.3 million tonnes, only around 225,000 is imported from the Gulf, and that too has been mainly imported by the private sector,” he said, adding that the ProGas terminal at Port Qasim was under the control of the Sui Southern Gas Company which “imported LPG around seven months back”. The association also wrote a letter to Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, stating the draft policy sent to the prime minister had no input from the private sector. The association called for the complete deregulation of the LPG sector. It said the 2016 LPG policy imposed Rs4,669 per tonne petroleum development levy on locally produced LPG. This was imposed to provide subsidies to the state-owned entities such as the PSO, Parco, and SSGC to import LPG during winters and in any emergency, like the current scenario. “Despite billions of rupees collected in terms of PDL through this formula, the state-owned entities have failed to import LPG during these days,” Mr Haider alleged. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Anti-party claims:Wike, Soludo, Adeleke fight back
items.description: •CSOs knock PDP, APGA, Accord leaders By Luminous Jannamike, Dickson Omobola, Henry Obeta & Esther Onyegbula The decision by some opposition governors to align with President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign has raised questions about party loyalty, political survival and the ability of opposition parties to present a united front ahead of the 2027 general election. At the centre of the unfolding political drama are the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, who remains a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP); Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA); and Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party. Findings by Sunday Vanguard showed that their political choices have placed their respective parties in a delicate position as they grapple with the implications of their members’ involvement in a campaign to return the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to power. Crisis Wike, a prominent PDP figure and former Rivers State governor, has maintained his support for Tinubu despite the protracted crisis within the PDP and his strained relationship with members of the party opposed to his position. Soludo, on his part, has had to navigate the implications of his political relationship with the President while remaining in APGA, a party with its own electoral ambitions and identity. Adeleke’s emergence under the Accord Party banner has also drawn attention to the political calculations surrounding his relationship with the Tinubu-led administration and the implications for his party. Although the circumstances surrounding the three politicians differ, their positions have triggered debate over whether opposition politicians can support the electoral ambitions of a rival party without undermining the platforms on which they built their political careers. Against the backdrop of the approaching 2027 elections, the development presents a test of the PDP, APGA and Accord Party’s capacity to manage internal disagreements, defend their political identities and determine the limits of acceptable conduct by their prominent members. It has also raised questions about the strength of party discipline in Nigeria, where political allegiances are frequently shaped by personal interests, strategic calculations and the search for relevance in the corridors of power. Also, many are unsure whether what the politicians have done amounts to anti-party activities. Constitution Accordingly, the constitutions of the affected parties, in various sections, spell out actions that could constitute anti-party activities. Specifically, Section 10(6) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Constitution provides that no member shall align with other parties or groups to undermine the party or any of its elected governments. The provision formed the basis of the party’s August 2025 warning against members publicly supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Section 59(1) was also cited by the party’s National Working Committee in issuing a reprimand over alleged anti-party activities. “The National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party has reviewed the anti-party activities of certain members of the Party, particularly those endorsing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for re-election in 2027,” the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Debo Ologunagba, warned. Also, Article 21 of the APGA Constitution, which deals with party discipline and disciplinary measures, provides for sanctions against members whose conduct brings the party into disrepute or ridicule. The provision requires members to maintain discipline in their public and private conduct. Like the PDP, APGA’s Anambra State chapter, in August 2022, specifically warned members against campaigning for candidates of other political parties, soliciting votes for them or promoting them on social media, describing such actions as anti-party activities. Similarly, Article 20(A)(vi) of the Accord Party Constitution, under discipline and offences, expressly identifies engaging in anti-party activities as an offence. Dismissed Article 14(3) also provides that a member may be dismissed by the appropriate party organ for anti-party activities, gross misconduct or violation of the constitution. These provisions establish a basis for disciplinary action against members found to have acted against the party’s interests. Adeleke’s spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, reportedly said: “We must avoid anti-party activities. Severe sanction awaits any party member who works against the candidates of the party.” Sunday Vanguard also observed that, irrespective of these provisions, Wike, Adeleke and Soludo have openly identified with President Tinubu’s campaign while still supporting other members vying for positions in their respective parties. For instance, Wike, who has openly declared support for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, described the emerging cross-party alliance as a “National Rainbow Coalition” involving politicians from different political platforms. On October 14, 2026, he attended the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council at the State House Conference Centre, Abuja, where he reaffirmed his support for Tinubu, citing the President’s handling of the country’s challenges. Wike was also named coordinator of Tinubu’s campaign in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory. He also disclosed in September that he had urged Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke to publicly reaffirm his support for Tinubu after winning re-election. Inauguration Similarly, Soludo, who attended the inauguration of the APC campaign council, declared that APGA would not field a presidential candidate in 2027, saying the party was supporting the government at the centre. He described Tinubu as his friend and said the President deserved a second term. The Anambra governor was subsequently appointed coordinator of the campaign in the state. Adeleke also publicly declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on October 14, 2026. Addressing the gathering, Adeleke pledged to mobilise support for Tinubu’s return to Aso Rock in 2027, saying: “I am here to throw my weight behind Tinubu’s return to Aso Rock. Let us rise from every nook and corner to support the President. Let him come and complete the good work he has begun.” The governor, popularly known for his energetic dance moves, subsequently joined Tinubu in dancing at the event, drawing cheers from the audience. The APC had named him coordinator of the President’s re-election campaign in Osun State. When Sunday Vanguard sought the positions of the concerned parties, they presented complex arguments, supporting the politicians while still insisting on party supremacy. Defence PDP spokesman Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, while defending Wike’s inclusion, argued that the minister had the right to decide whom he supported. He said: “Wike has every constitutional and democratic right to decide whom he supports politically. His support for President Tinubu is legitimate, and as a serving appointee of the President, there is nothing contradictory about supporting the President while maintaining his political identity and relationships within the PDP. “The FCT minister got the blessing of the PDP during the era of its former National Chairman, Umar Damagum, to work with Mr President. His inclusion in the Presidential Campaign Council was therefore expected, but this does not make him a member of the APC National Working Committee. “Every political party, including the PDP, would like to have Mr Nyesom Wike in their campaign council, but the party had already endorsed his invitation to help the current administration from day one. He is working for President Tinubu and not for APC.” In the same vein, APGA National Chairman, Sly Ezeokenwa, described Soludo’s case as a strategic alignment rather than a decision taken by the Anambra governor on his own. “The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), the National Working Committee, had already taken the decision that we will stay aligned and we will still share the same accord with the All Progressives Congress (APC) and accept the idea of adopting Mr President as our presidential candidate,” he said. Verdict Ezeokenwa argued that the arrangement served the interests of the South-East, suggesting that the region stood to gain from closer engagement with the Federal Government. On his part, Ogun State Chairman of the Accord Party, Michael Oke, told Sunday Vanguard that the national leadership learnt of Adeleke’s reported appointment through the media. Oke warned against reaching a verdict before the party had examined the circumstances and heard from those concerned. “Until the national leadership has studied the case and heard all concerned persons, it would be too early to conclude that the incident is anti-party,” Oke said. He cited Articles 13, 14 and 20 of the Accord Party Constitution, which he said deal with members’ obligations to comply with party decisions and provide for disciplinary action over anti-party activities or misconduct. Meanwhile, a chieftain of the party and member representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore Federal Constituency of Osun State, Bamidele Salam, described Adeleke’s appointment to lead Tinubu’s re-election campaign in Osun as a welcome development. The Imole Campaign Council (TICC) of Governor Adeleke also promised to deliver 1.5 million votes for Tinubu. In a statement, TICC Director-General, Olalere Oyewumi, described Adeleke’s appointment as well deserved, vowing that all Accord Party structures in Osun would work for Tinubu’s re-election. Oyewumi said Tinubu’s trust in Adeleke would be justified through unwavering commitment and a strong electoral performance. “The Imole Campaign Council welcomes the appointment of Governor Adeleke as State Coordinator of PBAT Presidential Campaign Council in Osun,” the statement added. A PDP chieftain, however, Chief Emmanuel Ogidi, accused Wike of maintaining a relationship with the PDP while allegedly supporting the interests of the APC, arguing that such conduct raised serious questions about loyalty and commitment to the opposition party. “You can’t serve two masters. He (Wike) is supposed to be serving us in PDP, but he is serving APC. This is a threat to democracy. APC is using him to destroy democracy, and it’s deliberate, but we are very conscious of that, and very soon you will hear what will happen,” Ogidi said. Values Meanwhile, some civil society organisations (CSOs), in conversations with Sunday Vanguard, disagreed with party leaders defending the development, arguing that the politicians’ actions amounted to anti-party activities that warranted disciplinary measures. Country Lead of the Society for Promotion of Democratic Values and Ethos, Dr Fredrick Manaseh, said the situation had significantly undermined party development and democratic values. He said: “Since the APC came to power, we have witnessed a systematic erosion of democratic values. The party, with its one-party-state agenda, has ensured that the growth of other parties is stunted. Regrettably, they have the likes of Wike and other politicians to promote that agenda. Therefore, let nobody deceive Nigerians, they are working against their parties and should receive disciplinary action.” Similarly, Executive Director of the Centre for Accountability and Good Governance, Prof Usman Monde, blamed political parties for failing to enforce their constitutional provisions. He said: “The answer to your question is obvious. They are rooting for other parties against the general wishes of their groups. Parties are governed by constitutions. When a party abandons its constitution because of the ambition of certain individuals within its fold, how can such a party grow and become competitive? “Political parties cannot claim to be serious about democracy if they fail to enforce their own rules. The constitution of a party should not apply only to ordinary members while prominent politicians are allowed to act as they please. There must be equal treatment and accountability for all members, irrespective of their status. “Where a party’s members openly support the presidential candidate of another party, the leadership must clarify whether such actions are consistent with its decisions and political objectives. If they are not, the appropriate disciplinary procedures should be invoked in accordance with the party’s constitution. “Democracy thrives when political parties have clear identities, competing visions and the discipline to hold their members accountable. When prominent members of opposition parties openly campaign for the re-election of the ruling party’s candidate, it raises legitimate questions about the opposition’s cohesion and capacity to offer Nigerians credible alternatives. “Ultimately, the responsibility rests with the leadership of these parties. They must demonstrate that their constitutions are binding on everyone, rather than allowing individual ambitions to override collective decisions. Without discipline, internal democracy and respect for party rules, political parties will struggle to build public confidence and remain competitive.” The post Anti-party claims:Wike, Soludo, Adeleke fight back appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests
items.description: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. He advised anyone experiencing symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, particularly after a relevant exposure, to seek immediate medical attention and disclose any relevant travel or contact history to healthcare workers. “Individuals should avoid self-medication and follow the advice of healthcare professionals,” he said. Idris said the NCDC, in collaboration with the Adamawa State Government and other relevant stakeholders, would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as verified information became available. He added that Nigeria’s public health authorities remained committed to protecting the population through early detection, evidence-based public health action, transparent communication and a coordinated national response. The post Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests appeared first on Vanguard News .
